# Sirach 15 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 15 (20 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 2

**Issue:** "Like a wife in her virginity" — how to render this image
- EMET: "like a wife in her virginity she will receive him"
- LOGOS: "like a wife married in virginity she will receive him"
- PNEUMA: "welcome them like a young bride"
- SOPHIA: "like a young bride she will receive him"

**Resolution:** Greek παρθενία = virginity/maidenhood. The image is of a beloved young wife. LOGOS "married in virginity" is awkward. PNEUMA "young bride" is clear. SOPHIA adopted PNEUMA's phrasing while retaining EMET's verb "receive." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 6

**Issue:** "Crown of rejoicing" vs. "crown of gladness"
- EMET: "a crown of rejoicing"
- LOGOS: "a crown of gladness"
- PNEUMA: "a crown of gladness"
- SOPHIA: "a crown of rejoicing"

**Resolution:** Greek ἀγαλλίαμα = exultation, great joy. Both "rejoicing" and "gladness" acceptable. EMET/SOPHIA "rejoicing" more dynamic. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 8

**Issue:** "Pride" vs. "arrogance" for ὑπερηφανία
- EMET: "far from pride"
- LOGOS: "far from arrogance"
- PNEUMA: "far from the arrogant"
- SOPHIA: "far from arrogance"

**Resolution:** Greek ὑπερηφανία = arrogance/haughtiness. LOGOS/SOPHIA "arrogance" preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 8b

**Issue:** "Liars will not remember her" vs. "deceivers will not think of her"
- EMET: "liars will not remember her"
- LOGOS: "deceivers will not think of her"
- PNEUMA: "liars never think of her"
- SOPHIA: "liars will not think of her"

**Resolution:** Greek ψευδεῖς = liars/false ones. "Think of" (LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA) slightly more natural than "remember." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 11

**Issue:** THE CRITICAL VERSE — attribution of sin to God
- EMET: "Do not say, 'It was because of the LORD that I turned away,' for you should not do what he hates"
- LOGOS: "Do not say, 'My turning away is from the LORD,' for he will not do what he hates"
- PNEUMA: "Don't say, 'God is the reason I went wrong' — he doesn't do what he hates"
- SOPHIA: "Do not say, 'It was the LORD's doing that I turned away,' for he does not do what he hates"

**Resolution:** This verse denies that God is responsible for human sin. The logical structure matters: the reason one cannot blame God is that God does not do what he hates. EMET's "you should not" shifts blame back to the speaker too directly. LOGOS/SOPHIA "he does not do" correctly identifies God as the subject of the refutation. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 12

**Issue:** "He led me astray" vs. "He caused me to stumble"
- EMET: "He led me astray"
- LOGOS: "He caused me to stumble"
- PNEUMA: "He led me astray"
- SOPHIA: "He caused me to stumble"

**Resolution:** Greek ἐξέκλινέν με = he made me deviate. Both renderings valid. "Stumble" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) fits the physical metaphor of v.11 (turning away). SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 14 — THE FREE WILL VERSE

**Issue:** "Left them in the hand of their own free choice" vs. "in the power of their own free choice"
- EMET: "left them in the hand of their own free choice"
- LOGOS: "left them in the hand of their own free choice"
- PNEUMA: "left them in the power of their own free choice"
- SOPHIA: "left them in the power of their own free choice"

**Resolution:** Greek ἐν χειρί = "in the hand" is the literal text. This verse (15:14) was central to the Pelagian controversy — Pelagius cited it to argue for unconstrained human free will. Augustine responded that "left them" implies original capacities before the Fall. The phrase ἐν χειρί (in the hand) is a Semitic idiom for being in someone's power/control. "In the hand" is most literal; "in the power" interprets the idiom. This is a theologically significant choice.

EMET/LOGOS retain "in the hand" (literal). PNEUMA/SOPHIA use "in the power" (idiomatic). SOPHIA chose to render the idiom meaningfully over strict literalism given the verse's theological weight, following PNEUMA. However, a footnote would ideally note the literal "in the hand." SOPHIA adopted with note.

**Council Note:** The phrase αὐτεξούσιον (free choice/self-determination) in 15:14 is one of the earliest uses of this philosophical term in Jewish wisdom literature. The SOPHIA rendering "left them in the power of their own free choice" deliberately renders the idiom idiomatically.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 15

**Issue:** "To act faithfully is a matter of your own decision" vs. "acting faithfully is a matter of your own will"
- EMET: "to act faithfully is a matter of your own decision"
- LOGOS: "acting faithfully is a matter of your own will"
- PNEUMA: "keeping faith is entirely your own decision"
- SOPHIA: "acting faithfully is a matter of your own will"

**Resolution:** Greek πίστις ποιῆσαι = to do faith/faithfulness. "Acting faithfully" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) more precise than "keeping faith" (PNEUMA). "Will" vs. "decision" — minor. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 16

**Issue:** "Stretch out your hand to whichever you wish"
- EMET: "stretch out your hand to whichever you wish"
- LOGOS: "stretch out your hand to whichever you will"
- PNEUMA: "reach out your hand to whichever you choose"
- SOPHIA: "stretch out your hand to whichever you will"

**Resolution:** "Will" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) maintains the thematic unity with v.15 and v.17 on will/choice. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 17

**Issue:** "Whichever one pleases him will be given to him"
- EMET: "whichever one pleases him will be given to him"
- LOGOS: "whichever one pleases them will be given to them"
- PNEUMA: "whichever one you desire is what you will receive"
- SOPHIA: "whichever one pleases them will be given to them"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA shifts to second person unnecessarily. LOGOS/SOPHIA use third person consistently. "Pleases" retained over "desire" (PNEUMA) as closer to Greek εὐδοκία. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 18

**Issue:** "Great is the wisdom of the LORD" — word order
- EMET: "great is the wisdom of the LORD"
- LOGOS: "the wisdom of the LORD is great"
- PNEUMA: "the wisdom of the LORD is immense"
- SOPHIA: "the wisdom of the LORD is great"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA "immense" is an intensification. LOGOS/SOPHIA order is more natural in English. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 19

**Issue:** "He knows every deed of man" — generic or specific
- EMET: "he knows every deed of man"
- LOGOS: "he knows every human deed"
- PNEUMA: "he knows everything that anyone does"
- SOPHIA: "he knows every human deed"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA "human deed" is less gendered than EMET "deed of man." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 20a

**Issue:** "Be ungodly" vs. "be wicked"
- EMET: "to be ungodly"
- LOGOS: "to be wicked"
- PNEUMA: "to be wicked"
- SOPHIA: "to be ungodly"

**Resolution:** Greek ἀσεβαίνειν = to act impiously/ungodly. EMET/SOPHIA "ungodly" preserves the religious connotation (impiety toward God) rather than general moral wickedness. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 20b

**Issue:** "Has not given permission" vs. "given no one license to sin"
- EMET: "has not given permission to anyone to sin"
- LOGOS: "has given no one permission to sin"
- PNEUMA: "has never given anyone license to sin"
- SOPHIA: "has given no one permission to sin"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA "license" has a more modern/legal ring that slightly departs from the direct denial. LOGOS/SOPHIA "permission" is clean. SOPHIA adopted.
